The frame line number in the FormatFieldError template differs between --a (line 12) and --b (line 13). A single shared error-formatting helper that hardcodes one number will be wrong half the time.

The switch is on the length of the first maximal run of bad bytes, not on the total count of bad bytes.
Only the FIRST run of unencodable code points is reported. `a\xffb\xfec` must report position 1 and stop scanning — do not report the last one or a combined range.

Every invalid byte becomes exactly ONE surrogate code point — the run length equals the count of consecutive bytes not consumed by a valid sequence. `c2 41` gives a run of 1 (singular form) because the `41` is valid ASCII, while `f0 9f 41` gives a run of 2. The condition is exactly `hasSQ && !hasDQ` -> double quote. It is NOT `hasSQ -> double quote`. When BOTH are present Python uses SINGLE quotes and escapes the apostrophes: b'both\'"x'. A common wrong implementation picks double quotes whenever an apostrophe exists.

Byte 0x22 (") is never escaped. Do not add a `if (c===0x22) s += '\\"'` branch that fires when the delimiter is a double quote — it is dead code, but if you also mis-derive the delimiter it will produce wrong output. Inside single quotes, " is emitted raw.
Only \t, \n, \r are named. JS developers reflexively add \b, \f, \v, \0 (all of which JS's own escape conventions have). Python emits \x08, \x0c, \x0b, \x00 for those. Also no octal escapes.
Hex must be LOWERCASE and zero-padded to exactly 2 digits: use c.toString(16).padStart(2,'0'). `toString(16).toUpperCase()` or unpadded output (\x7 instead of \x07) both diverge.
0x7f (DEL) is escaped (\x7f) even though it is < 0x80. The printable range is 0x20..0x7e INCLUSIVE on both ends; the test must be `c >= 0x20 && c <= 0x7e`, i.e. `c < 0x20 || c >= 0x7f` -> hex.

gotchas: The `-5` rule. A naive JS port will treat any token starting with '-' as an option and emit "expected one argument". WRONG: a token matching /^-\d+$/ or /^-\d*\.\d+$/ is a VALUE. `--c -5` -> b'-5', `--a -3` -> construct traceback. But `-5.` and `-5e3` are options (-> "expected one argument"). Test all six forms.
The bare `-` rule. A token of exactly one character (`-`) is NEVER an option. `--c -` -> b'-'. Naive ports emit "expected one argument".

The SPACE rule. Any token containing a space is NEVER an option, even if it starts with `--`. `--c '--z x'` -> b'--z x' (success). `'--a 1'` as one token becomes an unrecognized positional, NOT an --a option.

Extras keep `--` verbatim. Because this parser has ZERO positional actions, argparse never strips the `--` separator; it lands in the unrecognized list. `--a 1 --b 2 --c x -- foo` -> "unrecognized arguments: -- foo", not "foo". A naive port that drops `--` will diverge.

-h peels out of a short cluster. `-hx` and `-h5` PRINT HELP and exit 0 (argparse splits `-h` off, pushes `-x`/`-5` to extras, then the help action fires and exits before extras are reported). But `-h=1` errors with "argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '1'". The discriminator is whether the separator was an '=' (or the tail starts with '-').

The ambiguous-option case is reachable: `--=` and `--=1` split on '=' to the prefix `--`, which prefix-matches all four long options -> "ambiguous option: --=1 could match --help, --a, --b, --c". Candidate order is declaration order with --help FIRST (from -h/--help being added first), and the message echoes the ORIGINAL token including the '=part'.

Precedence is order-sensitive for -h. `-h --a abc` -> help (exit 0). `--a abc -h` -> invalid-int error (exit 2). You must parse strictly left-to-right and fire errors/actions at the moment the token is consumed, not in a post-pass.
Required-missing beats unrecognized-extras, always. But BOTH are post-parse, so any parse-time error (invalid int, expected one argument, ambiguous, ignored explicit) beats both.

Two different escaping regimes on stderr. "invalid int value: X" uses Python repr() (quotes, \t, \n, \xNN, \udcNN). "unrecognized arguments: ..." uses RAW text joined by a single space -- a tab is a real tab byte, a newline is a real newline that splits the output across lines. Do not repr the extras.

Non-ASCII in repr(): printable Unicode stays literal (é, 😀, U+0301 combining acute), but non-printable Unicode is escaped -- NBSP U+00A0 renders as \xa0 because Python treats Zs (other than space) as non-printable. A JS port using a naive /[^\x20-\x7e]/ escape would wrongly escape é and 😀; one using no escaping would wrongly emit a literal NBSP.

Invalid-UTF-8 argv bytes become U+DCxx surrogates. In repr() they show as '\udcff' (from repr's escaping); in the raw extras list they show as the literal ASCII text \udcff too, because stderr uses errors='backslashreplace'. Node's process.argv gives U+FFFD instead -- read /proc/self/cmdline (NUL-separated) with node:fs to recover the real bytes.

The help block's second line is a completely EMPTY line (just \n), and the rows `  --a A` / `  --b B` / `  --c C` have NO padding to column 14 and NO trailing whitespace -- only the -h row is padded. Total help output is exactly 127 bytes.
Empty-string extra produces a line with a trailing space: "test8_executable: error: unrecognized arguments: " + "\n". Easy to lose if you trim.

COLUMNS changes wrapping (width = COLUMNS-2; usage wraps when COLUMNS < 48). If the reference harness sets COLUMNS you must emulate the wrap algorithm; if it doesn't, hardcode 80. COLUMNS=0/empty/non-numeric falls back to 80. The `test8_executable: error: ...` line is NEVER wrapped either way.

`--a` / `--b` / `--c` abbreviation: `--ab` matches nothing (it is longer than `--a`, not a prefix of it) and becomes an unrecognized extra -- but `--a` then reports as MISSING REQUIRED, which fires first, so the visible message is "the following arguments are required: --a", not "unrecognized arguments: --ab 1".

gotchas: ARGV MUST BE READ AS RAW BYTES. Node's process.argv replaces invalid UTF-8 with U+FFFD, which changes both accept/reject behaviour and the repr text. Read /proc/self/cmdline with node:fs (NUL-separated), split, and decode each argument with a surrogateescape-compatible decoder that maps each undecodable byte B to U+DC00+B. Only then do repr and int() match ('a\xffb' must print 'a\udcffb', not 'a�b').

ITERATE BY CODE POINT, NOT UTF-16 UNIT. Astral Nd digits (U+104A0, U+1D7CE-1D7FF, U+1FBF0-1FBF9, U+1E4F0-1E4F9, U+11F50-11F59) are real digits; a charCodeAt-based loop sees two surrogates and will reject them. Use [...str] / codePointAt.

THE WHITESPACE SET IS NOT /\s/ AND NOT str.isspace(). ASCII 0x1C-0x1F ARE Python str.isspace() but are NOT stripped by int() (CPython's transform only rewrites non-ASCII, then uses C isspace). Conversely U+0085 and U+00A0 ARE stripped even though JS /\s/ ... actually JS /\s/ does match   and ﻿ — and U+FEFF must be REJECTED. So neither String.prototype.trim() nor /\s/ is correct. Hardcode: ASCII {09,0A,0B,0C,0D,20} plus {0085,00A0,1680,2000-200A,2028,2029,202F,205F,3000}. Note JS trim() strips U+FEFF (wrong) and does strip U+2028/2029/00A0 (right).
JS trim() also strips U+FEFF, so `s.trim()` would accept '﻿5' which the reference REJECTS. Write an explicit trim.

UNICODE DIGIT MAPPING IS THE FULL Nd CATEGORY, NOT JUST 0-9. Use a code-point-range table of Nd blocks (each block's zero is at a known offset; value = cp - blockZero). JS \d and Number()/parseInt() only handle ASCII. Also make sure the table is Unicode 15.x: U+10D40-10D49 (Garay, Unicode 16) must NOT be treated as digits — the reference rejects them and reprs U+10D40 as '\U00010d40' (unassigned).

DO NOT USE Number/parseInt/parseFloat. parseInt('0x10') = 16, Number(' ') = 0, Number('1e2') = 100, parseInt('12abc') = 12 — all wrong here. Parse with a strict regex and build the magnitude with BigInt.
VALUES ARE ARBITRARY PRECISION. '99999999999999999999' must round-trip exactly in the 'given value <N>' traceback line; Number loses precision at 2^53. Use BigInt and BigInt.prototype.toString().

THE 4300-DIGIT CAP IS EASY TO MISS AND EASY TO GET WRONG: count only digit characters (leading zeros included), excluding sign, whitespace and underscores. 4300 passes, 4301 fails, and the failure is the plain 'invalid int value' message (exit 2), not a distinct error.

STR REPR != BYTES REPR. \v and \f are NOT named escapes in either, but str repr uses \xNN/\uNNNN/\UNNNNNNNN based on CODE POINT (not byte), and printable non-ASCII (é, 😀, ！) is emitted LITERALLY as UTF-8. A naive port that escapes everything >= 0x80 produces 'x\xc3\xa9y' instead of 'xéy'.

PRINTABILITY IS A UNICODE CATEGORY TEST, NOT /[\x20-\x7e]/. Non-printable = general category Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, Zs, except U+0020 which IS printable. You need a code-point range table for this (Cn/unassigned is the big one). Watch the surprises: U+034F (Mn) prints literally, U+3164 and U+115F print literally, U+FFFD prints literally, but U+00AD, U+061C, U+200B, U+200E, U+202A, U+2060, U+FFF9, U+FEFF, U+1D173, U+E0001 are all escaped.

REPR ESCAPE WIDTH IS BY CODE POINT VALUE: <=0xFF -> \xNN, <=0xFFFF -> \uNNNN, else \UNNNNNNNN, always lowercase hex, zero-padded. A JS port that escapes per UTF-16 unit would print '𝅳' where Python prints '\U0001d173' — but note lone surrogates from surrogateescape DO print as '\udcff' individually.
ARGUMENT CONVERSION ORDER: --a is converted first, then --b, then --c; the program exits on the FIRST failure. '--a abc --b def' reports --a only.
The error text never truncates the repr, even for a 5000-character argument.

gotchas: Position in the UnicodeEncodeError message is a PYTHON CODE POINT index. In JS, `str.length` and `str[i]` are UTF-16 units, so an astral character before the bad byte shifts the number by one. Always iterate with `[...str]` / a for..of loop and use `[...str].length` for Python's len(). Verified: --c $'A\xf0\x9f\x98\x80B\xffC' reports position 3, but 'A\u{1F600}B\uDCFFC'.length is 5 and indexOf-style math would say 4.

A naive port using `new TextDecoder('utf-8')` (or process.argv directly) collapses each maximal invalid subpart to ONE U+FFFD. Python emits one surrogate PER BYTE. $'\xe2\x82' -> 1 char in Node vs 2 chars in Python, so both the reported position range AND the StreamError 'expected N' length would be wrong. You must hand-roll the decoder with byte-by-byte resync.

`new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal:true})` is also unusable as a shortcut: it throws without telling you where, and it accepts nothing you can resync on. Write the explicit lead-byte/continuation table (C2-DF/E0-EF/F0-F4 with the E0>=A0, ED<=9F, F0>=90, F4<=8F second-byte constraints).

Escaped bytes are produced with String.fromCharCode(0xDC00 + b), which makes a LONE low surrogate. The resulting JS string is not well-formed UTF-16. Never round-trip it through Buffer.from(s,'utf8'), TextEncoder, JSON.stringify-then-parse, or `console.log` of the raw string: all of those silently replace it with U+FFFD (EF BF BD) and you lose the exact byte. Keep such strings internal and only ever render them via the explicit \\udcNN escaping logic.

Detecting a lone surrogate must not be done with charCodeAt on a well-formed pair. Iterate with [...str]: a valid astral char yields one element with codePointAt() >= 0x10000, a lone surrogate yields one element with codePointAt() in 0xD800..0xDFFF. Testing charCodeAt(i) in D800-DFFF would false-positive on every emoji.

process.argv.length - 2 is the user-arg count only when the entry really is a script file. Under `node -e` there is no script argv slot, so the count would be off by one and the tail slice would silently steal a wrong entry. The lossy TextDecoder cross-check against process.argv catches this; keep it.

Do NOT try to align /proc/self/cmdline by locating process.argv[1] in it. Node resolves the script to an absolute path while cmdline preserves whatever the shell passed ('t.mjs' vs '/tmp/rev/t.mjs'). Tail-align by count instead. Verified working with a relative script path.

When splitting cmdline on NUL, an off-by-one is easy: the buffer ends with a NUL terminator, so a naive `String.split('\0')` or a loop that also pushes a final tail always yields one extra empty entry — which then makes a legitimate trailing empty-string argument indistinguishable. Correct pattern: push a slice at every NUL, and push a final slice only if start < bytes.length. Tested with a trailing '' argument.

statSync('/proc/self/cmdline').size is 0. Any code that pre-allocates by stat size, or that bails on size===0, will read nothing. readFileSync handles it correctly (verified up to a 60003-byte argument, no 4096-byte truncation).

readFileSync returns a Buffer whose .slice() is a VIEW, not a copy. Convert once with Uint8Array.from(buf) so subsequent .slice() calls are %TypedArray%.slice copies. (This also keeps you clear of the banned typed-array-backing-store APIs — never touch .buffer.)

stderr uses backslashreplace, so unencodable code points in the 'unrecognized arguments:' path print as literal \\udcNN text, but valid non-ASCII (e.g. e-acute) prints as RAW UTF-8 bytes. A port that escapes all non-ASCII on stderr would be wrong; a port that escapes nothing would also be wrong. Only lone surrogates get the \\udcNN treatment there.

Two different mechanisms produce the same \\udcNN text: repr() on the 'invalid int value:' path (which also escapes \\x01, \\t, etc.) versus stderr backslashreplace on the 'unrecognized arguments:' path (which passes raw control bytes through untouched). Proven with $'x\x01y': repr path prints 'x\\x01y', raw path prints a literal 0x01 byte. Don't unify the two code paths.

For --c, success is possible ONLY if every byte is 0x01..0x7F. Any high byte guarantees exit 1. A port can rely on this but must still pick the RIGHT error (StreamError vs UnicodeEncodeError) — UnicodeEncodeError wins whenever any lone surrogate is present, because .encode() runs before construct.

The argparse prog name comes from basename(sys.argv[0]), not a constant — an exec -a rename changes it. A Node port must hardcode "test8_executable", because basename(process.argv[1]) would give "test8.mjs".

The locale here is POSIX/C (LANG and LC_ALL empty) yet Python still uses UTF-8 + surrogateescape for argv, thanks to PEP 538/540 coercion. Don't assume a latin-1 or ASCII argv decoding just because the locale is C.

# test8 → Node.js Port: Authoritative Implementation Spec

**Target:** byte-exact behavioural clone of `/workspace/dataset/test8_executable` in pure Node.js (v18.19.1).
**Entry point:** `/output/test8.mjs`. **Library:** `/output/lib/**.mjs`.

Everything below is normative. Where the five specialists disagreed or left gaps, §9 states the resolution — I re-ran the reference binary to settle the contested points, and those transcripts are quoted inline.

---

## 0. Hard constraints (restated — these are absolute)

* **ESM only.** `import` / `export`. `require()` and `module.exports` are **forbidden**.
* **Every file ends in `.mjs`**, and **every relative import spells the extension**: `import { x } from './lib/py/strRepr.mjs';`.
* **Zero npm/external dependencies.** Only relative imports and `node:` builtins (`node:fs`, `node:process`).
* **Never use, import, or mention `DataView` or `ArrayBuffer`** — not in code, not in comments, not in identifiers. Build binary data with `Uint8Array.from(...)`, `Uint8Array.of(...)`, `new Uint8Array(n)`, or plain number arrays. **Never touch `.buffer`** on a typed array.
* **No Python.** No embedded interpreter, no `child_process`, no shelling out.
* Hierarchical decomposition: focused modules under `/output/lib/`, wired by `/output/test8.mjs`.
* The program name is the hardcoded literal string `test8_executable` (see §9.1).

---

## 1. Module tree and exported interfaces

```
/output/test8.mjs                      # entry point: wiring + top-level control flow only
/output/lib/
  runtime/
    streams.mjs                        # raw byte writes to fd 1/2, Python stream encodings, exit
    rawArgv.mjs                        # /proc/self/cmdline recovery of raw argv bytes
  py/
    unicode.mjs                        # code-point iteration + Unicode predicates/tables
    codec.mjs                          # surrogateescape decode, strict UTF-8 encode, backslashreplace
    intParse.mjs                       # CPython int(str) semantics
    strRepr.mjs                        # CPython repr(str)
    bytesRepr.mjs                      # CPython repr(bytes)
  argparse/
    spec.mjs                           # prog name, option table, static text constants
    format.mjs                         # terminal width, usage line, full help block, wrapping
    errors.mjs                         # control-flow exception types
    parser.mjs                         # the parser (pre-pass + left-to-right consumption)
  construct/
    errors.mjs                         # FormatFieldError / StreamError value objects
    int8ul.mjs                         # Int8ul.build
    bytesfield.mjs                     # Bytes(n).build
  traceback/
    templates.mjs                      # the three exact stderr traceback renderings
```

### 1.1 `lib/runtime/streams.mjs`

```js
export function writeBytes(fd, bytes)        // bytes: Uint8Array | number[]  -> fs.writeSync loop until fully written
export function writeStdoutBytes(bytes)      // fd 1
export function writeStderrBytes(bytes)      // fd 2
export function writeStderrPyText(str)       // encode with backslashreplace (py/codec) then writeStderrBytes
export function writeStdoutAscii(str)        // str is guaranteed pure ASCII; encode 1 byte per char
export function exitWith(code)               // process.exit(code) AFTER all synchronous writes
```

Semantics: all writes are **synchronous** (`fs.writeSync`) so nothing can be lost when `process.exit` runs. `writeBytes` must loop on partial writes. Never pass a JS string to `fs.writeSync` for stderr content — strings containing lone surrogates would be mangled to U+FFFD; always hand it a `Uint8Array` you built yourself.

### 1.2 `lib/runtime/rawArgv.mjs`

```js
export function getArgvByteArrays()   // -> Array<Uint8Array>, one per user argument (argv[2..])
```

Algorithm (fully specified in §2.1). Never throws; falls back to a lossy encoding of `process.argv.slice(2)`.

### 1.3 `lib/py/unicode.mjs`

```js
export function codePoints(str)        // -> number[]  (uses [...str], i.e. code points, incl. lone surrogates)
```

## 2. Precise algorithms

### 2.1 Raw argv recovery (`rawArgv.mjs`)

Node's `process.argv` replaces invalid UTF-8 bytes with U+FFFD (WHATWG maximal-subpart), destroying both the byte identity and the **count** of bad code points. Recover the raw bytes:

1. `let buf; try { buf = readFileSync('/proc/self/cmdline'); } catch { return fallback(); }`
   Convert once: `const bytes = Uint8Array.from(buf);` (Buffer `.slice()` is a view; `Uint8Array.prototype.slice` copies. Never touch `.buffer`.)
   Note `statSync(...).size === 0` for this file — **never** pre-size or bail on size 0. `readFileSync` returns the full contents (verified up to 60 KB arguments; no 4096-byte truncation).
2. Split on `0x00`: `entries=[]; let start=0; for (let i=0;i<bytes.length;i++) if (bytes[i]===0) { entries.push(bytes.slice(start,i)); start=i+1; } if (start < bytes.length) entries.push(bytes.slice(start));`
   This consumes the trailing NUL terminator **without** dropping a legitimate trailing empty argument.
3. `const want = process.argv.length - 2; if (want < 0 || entries.length < want) return fallback();`
4. Tail-align: `const tail = entries.slice(entries.length - want);` — **never** try to locate `process.argv[1]` inside cmdline (Node absolutizes the script path; the shell may have passed a relative one).
5. Cross-check: for each `i`, `new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(tail[i]) === process.argv[i+2]`. Any mismatch → `fallback()`. (Node's own lossy substitution matches `TextDecoder` exactly in every tested case, so a mismatch reliably means misalignment, e.g. `node -e`.)
6. `fallback()` = `process.argv.slice(2).map(s => new TextEncoder().encode(s))` — byte-exact for all valid UTF-8 input; degrades to U+FFFD only for invalid-UTF-8 input.

Tail-alignment was verified robust across: node exec flags, `NODE_OPTIONS`, relative script paths, symlinked node, `sh -c` wrappers, `exec -a` argv0 spoofing, zero args, empty-string args (interior and trailing), args containing spaces, and args equal to the script path.

### 2.2 surrogateescape decode (`decodeSurrogateEscape`)

Byte-by-byte resync decoder. **Not** maximal-subpart:

```
i = 0; out = []
while i < n:
  b = bytes[i]
  if b < 0x80:                              push b;                 i += 1; continue
  seq = null
  if 0xC2 <= b <= 0xDF: seq = 2
  else if 0xE0 <= b <= 0xEF: seq = 3
  else if 0xF0 <= b <= 0xF4: seq = 4
  valid = seq !== null && i + seq <= n
  if valid:
     all trailing bytes must be 0x80..0xBF
     extra second-byte constraints:  b==0xE0 -> [0xA0..0xBF];  b==0xED -> [0x80..0x9F]
                                     b==0xF0 -> [0x90..0xBF];  b==0xF4 -> [0x80..0x8F]
  if valid: decode cp, push cp, i += seq
  else:     push 0xDC00 + b, i += 1          # exactly ONE surrogate per bad byte, advance ONE byte
```

Leads `0x80..0xC1` and `0xF5..0xFF` are always invalid. This exactly reproduces CPython: `c2 41` → 1 surrogate then `A`; `f0 9f 41` → 2 surrogates then `A`; `e0 9f 41` → 2 surrogates then `A`; `e2 82` → 2 surrogates; `f8 88 80 80 80` → 5 surrogates. Overlongs (`c0 80`, `e0 80 80`, `f0 80 80 80`), encoded surrogates (`ed a0 80`..`ed bf bf`) and `> U+10FFFF` (`f4 90 80 80`, `f5 80 80 80`) are rejected per-byte; `ed 9f bf` (U+D7FF), `f4 8f bf bf` (U+10FFFF), `ef bf bd` (U+FFFD) are **valid**.

Build the string with `String.fromCodePoint(...)`; lone surrogates produce a non-well-formed UTF-16 string. **Keep it internal**: never round-trip it through `TextEncoder`, `Buffer.from(s,'utf8')`, `JSON.stringify`/`parse`, `console.log`, or template-literal output — every one of those silently substitutes U+FFFD.

### 2.3 `encodeUtf8Strict` (Python `str.encode()`)

Iterate **code points**, tracking a code-point index `k`:

* First code point with `0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF` starts the error run at `start = k`; extend `end` while the *next* code points are also surrogates. Return `{ok:false, start, end, cp: cpAtStart}` immediately — only the **first** run is ever reported.
* Otherwise emit standard UTF-8 (1/2/3/4 bytes) into a number array; return `{ok:true, bytes: Uint8Array.from(arr)}`.

### 2.4 `encodeBackslashReplace` (Python stderr encoding)

For each code point: if it is a lone surrogate (`0xD800..0xDFFF`), emit the **literal ASCII text** `\udcNN` (backslash, `u`, 4 lowercase hex digits, zero-padded); otherwise emit its UTF-8 bytes verbatim. Valid non-ASCII (é, 😀) goes out as raw UTF-8. Raw control bytes (e.g. 0x01) pass through **unescaped** on this path.

### 2.5 Python `int(str)` (`pyInt`)

Operate on **code points**.

1. **Map** each code point `cp`:
   * `cp < 0x7F` → keep unchanged
   * else if `isPyIntSpace(cp)` → `0x20`
   * else if `ndDigitValue(cp) !== null` → `0x30 + ndDigitValue(cp)`
   * else → keep unchanged (it will fail the regex)
   (`0x7F` DEL is *not* `< 0x7F`, is neither space nor digit, so it survives and rejects. Correct.)
2. **Strip** leading and trailing code points in `{0x09,0x0A,0x0B,0x0C,0x0D,0x20}` **only** (C `isspace`). `0x1C..0x1F` are *not* stripped and therefore reject.
3. **Match** `/^[+-]?[0-9](_?[0-9])*$/` on the stripped mapped string. Fail → `{ok:false}`.
   (This permits `1_0_0_0`; it forbids `_1`, `1_`, `1__0`, `+_10`, and any sign not immediately followed by a digit.)
4. **Digit cap:** count characters `[0-9]` in the stripped string (leading zeros counted; sign, underscores, whitespace not). `> 4300` → `{ok:false}`. (4300 accepts, 4301 rejects.)
5. **Value:** remove `_`, then `BigInt(s)`. `BigInt("+5") === 5n`, `BigInt("007") === 7n`, `BigInt("-0") === 0n` — all verified in Node 18.19.1. Return `{ok:true, value}`.

**Never** use `Number`, `parseInt`, `parseFloat`, `trim()`, `/\s/`, or `\d` for any of this.

Canonical decimal for the traceback (`given value {VALUE}`) is `value.toString()` on the BigInt — `+256`→`256`, `000000256`→`256`, `1_0_0_0`→`1000`, `  -300  `→`-300`, `٩٩٩`→`999`, and arbitrary precision preserved (`-99999999999999999999999999`).

### 2.6 Python `repr(str)` (`pyStrRepr`) — used only in `invalid int value: X`

1. **Quote selection** over the whole string, before escaping: `hasSQ = contains U+0027`, `hasDQ = contains U+0022`. Delimiter = `"` **iff** `hasSQ && !hasDQ`; otherwise `'`.
2. For each **code point**, in this priority order:
   1. `cp === 0x27` and delimiter is `'` → `\'`
   2. `cp === 0x5C` → `\\`
   3. `cp === 0x09` → `\t`; `0x0A` → `\n`; `0x0D` → `\r` (these are the **only** named escapes — no `\a \b \f \v \0`, no octal)
   4. `isPyPrintable(cp)` → the literal character
   5. else → `cp <= 0xFF` ? `\xNN` : `cp <= 0xFFFF` ? `\uNNNN` : `\UNNNNNNNN` — lowercase hex, zero-padded to 2/4/8
3. `U+0022` is never escaped.

Consequences to honour: `é`, `😀`, `！`, `U+034F`, `U+3164`, `U+115F`, `U+FFFD` print **literally** (as UTF-8 on the wire); `U+00A0`→`\xa0`, `U+00AD`→`\xad`, `U+0085`→`\x85`, `U+061C`/`U+200B`/`U+200E`/`U+202A`/`U+2060`/`U+FFF9`/`U+FEFF` → escaped; `U+1D173`→`\U0001d173`; `U+E0001`→`\U000e0001`; `U+0378`, `U+10D40` → `\uNNNN`/`\UNNNNNNNN` (unassigned); lone surrogates → `\udcNN`.

### 2.7 Python `repr(bytes)` (`pyBytesRepr`)

1. Two-pass. Scan the **byte** sequence: `hasSQ = contains 0x27`, `hasDQ = contains 0x22`. Delimiter = `"` iff `hasSQ && !hasDQ`, else `'`. Empty sequence → `'` → `b''`.
2. Emit `b`, delimiter, then per byte `c`:
   1. `c === 0x27 && delim === "'"` → `\'`
   2. `c === 0x5C` → `\\` (unconditionally, including inside a double-quoted repr)
   3. `c === 0x09` → `\t`; `0x0A` → `\n`; `0x0D` → `\r`
   4. `c < 0x20 || c >= 0x7F` → `\x` + `c.toString(16).padStart(2,'0')` (lowercase, always 2 digits — `0x7F` included)
   5. else (`0x20..0x7E`) → the literal ASCII character (this includes `"`)
3. Emit the delimiter. Output is always pure ASCII. No wrapping, no truncation, ever.

This table was differentially verified against all 256 byte values and 65 fuzz strings.

### 2.8 `construct` builds

* `buildInt8ul(v: BigInt)`: `if (v < 0n || v > 255n) throw new FormatFieldError(v.toString());` else `return Uint8Array.of(Number(v));`
* `buildBytes(n, data)`: `if (data.length !== n) throw new StreamError(n, data.length);` else `return data;`
* `n` is `pyLen(c)` = **code-point count** of the `--c` string, never `.length`.

### 2.9 argparse

#### 2.9.1 Token classification (`_parse_optional` equivalent), in this exact order

Given token `t`, return one of: `POSITIONAL`, `{action, optionString, sep, explicitArg}`, `UNKNOWN_OPTION`, or raise `AMBIGUOUS`.

1. `t === ''` → POSITIONAL.
2. `t[0] !== '-'` → POSITIONAL.
3. `t` is exactly one of `-h`, `--help`, `--a`, `--b`, `--c` → that action, `sep=null`, `explicitArg=null`.
4. `t.length === 1` (i.e. `-`) → POSITIONAL.
5. If `t` contains `=`: split on the **first** `=` into `head`/`rest`. If `head` is an exact known option string → that action with `sep='='`, `explicitArg=rest` (rest may be empty, may contain `=` or dashes).
6. Prefix matching:
   * `t` starts with `--`: let `optPrefix` = (`=` present ? `head` : `t`), `explicit` = (`=` present ? `rest` : `null`). Candidates = every long option in `LONG_OPTION_ORDER` that `startsWith(optPrefix)`.
   * `t` starts with a single `-`: candidate if `optionString === t.slice(0,2)` (then `sep=''`, `explicitArg = t.slice(2)`), or if `optionString.startsWith(t)`.
   * `candidates.length > 1` → **AMBIGUOUS**: `ambiguous option: {t} could match {candidates joined ", "}` (candidate order = declaration order `--help, --a, --b, --c`; the message echoes the **original** token including the `=part`).
   * `candidates.length === 1` → that candidate.
7. Negative-number test: `/^-\d+$/` or `/^-\d*\.\d+$/` (Python `\d` = Unicode `Nd`; use `isDecimalDigitCp`) → POSITIONAL. (`-5`, `-12345`, `-5.5`, `-.5` are values; `-5.` and `-5e3` are not.)
8. `t` contains a space (`' '`) → POSITIONAL. (`'--z x'` and `'--a 1'` as single tokens are positionals.)
9. Otherwise → UNKNOWN_OPTION (goes to extras verbatim).

#### 2.9.2 Pre-pass (this is where the ambiguous error fires)

Before any consumption, walk the tokens left to right and build a pattern array:

* If a token is exactly `--` **and this is the first such token**: mark it `'-'` and mark **every remaining token** `'A'` without classifying them (so no ambiguity check happens after `--`), then stop the pre-pass.
* Otherwise classify per §2.9.1; `POSITIONAL` → `'A'`, anything option-like → `'O'`; an `AMBIGUOUS` result **immediately** raises `ArgparseError` (leftmost ambiguous token wins).

**This pre-pass beats everything**, including `-h` and invalid ints. Verified:

```
$ ./test8_executable --a abc --=1  -> error: ambiguous option: --=1 could match --help, --a, --b, --c   (exit 2)
$ ./test8_executable -h --=1       -> same ambiguous error (NOT help)
$ ./test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c x -- --=1 -> error: unrecognized arguments: -- --=1   (after `--`, no ambiguity check)
$ ./test8_executable --a 1 --b 2 --c=--=1      -> exit 0, b'\x01' / b'\x02' / b'--=1'
```

#### 2.9.3 Consumption (strict left-to-right)

State: `values = {}`, `extras = []`, `i = 0`.

* If `pattern[i] === '-'` (the separator): push `--` **and every remaining token verbatim** onto `extras`; stop parsing. The `--` is never stripped (there are zero positional actions).
* If `pattern[i] === 'A'`: `extras.push(token); i++`.
* If `pattern[i] === 'O'`:
  * **UNKNOWN_OPTION**: `extras.push(token); i++`. (Its following value token, if any, is an `'A'` and lands in extras too — `--z 5` → `unrecognized arguments: --z 5`.)
  * **help action** (`-h`/`--help`, nargs 0):
    * `explicitArg === null` → throw `HelpRequested` **immediately** (exit 0; later errors and extras are never reported).
    * `explicitArg !== null`:
      * If `sep === '='` **or** `explicitArg === ''` **or** `explicitArg[0] === '-'` → `ArgparseError("argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument " + pyStrRepr(explicitArg))`. Note the action name is the joined `-h/--help`.
      * Else (short cluster, e.g. `-hx`, `-h5`): the help action fires anyway → throw `HelpRequested`. (argparse peels `-h` off, pushes `-x` to extras, then the action exits before extras are reported.) Verified: `-hx` and `-h5` exit 0 with the full help.
  * **`--a` / `--b` / `--c`** (nargs 1):
    * Value = `explicitArg` when it is non-null (the `=` form — this bypasses the option-lookalike check entirely, so `--c=-x`, `--c=--b`, `--c=--` all work).
    * Otherwise: if `i+1 < n` **and** `pattern[i+1] === 'A'` → value = `token[i+1]`, `i += 2`. Else → `ArgparseError("argument " + optionString + ": expected one argument")`. (A next token classified `'O'` or the `'-'` separator, or no next token at all, all produce this.)
    * **Convert immediately, at consumption time**: for `--a`/`--b`, `pyInt(value)`; on failure → `ArgparseError("argument " + optionString + ": invalid int value: " + pyStrRepr(value))`. For `--c`, store the string unchanged.
    * Store into `values` (**last occurrence wins**).

#### 2.9.4 Post-parse checks, in this order

1. **Missing required**: collect the missing among `--a`, `--b`, `--c` in **declaration order** (independent of argv order) → `ArgparseError("the following arguments are required: " + missing.join(', '))`.
2. **Unrecognized**: if `extras.length` → `ArgparseError("unrecognized arguments: " + extras.join(' '))`. Extras are **raw** — no repr, no quoting, no escaping (an interior tab is a real tab; an empty extra yields a trailing space).

Precedence summary (highest first): **ambiguous option (pre-pass)** → any parse-time error or `-h` in left-to-right token order → missing-required → unrecognized-extras → construct errors.

### 2.10 Usage and help text generation

`terminalColumns()`: `COLUMNS` env var parsed as an integer; used only if it parses and is `>= 1`; otherwise **80**. (`COLUMNS=0`, empty, or non-numeric → 80.) `width = columns - 2`.

At the default width 78, `formatHelp(78)` **must** produce exactly this 127-byte string (verified `wc -c` = 127; line 2 is truly empty; no trailing spaces anywhere; exactly one final `\n`):

```
usage: test8_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n  --a A\n  --b B\n  --c C\n
```

and `formatUsage(78)` = `usage: test8_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C` (46 chars, no newline).

**Usage algorithm** (`prefix = "usage: "`, `prog = "test8_executable"`, `usageBody = "[-h] --a A --b B --c C"`):

* If `prefix.length + usageBody.length <= width` → single line `prefix + usageBody`. (Fits iff `width >= 46`, i.e. `COLUMNS >= 48`.)
* Else split the body into whitespace-delimited parts: `['[-h]','--a','A','--b','B','--c','C']` (argparse's `\S+` split — note `--a A` becomes **two** parts).
  * `getLines(parts, indent, isFirstWithPrefix)`: `lineLen = (isFirstWithPrefix ? prefix.length : indent.length) - 1`; for each part, if `lineLen + 1 + part.length > width && line.length` → flush `indent + line.join(' ')`, reset `lineLen = indent.length - 1`; then `line.push(part); lineLen += 1 + part.length`. Flush the remainder. If `isFirstWithPrefix`, strip `indent.length` leading chars from line 0.
  * If `prefix.length + prog.length <= 0.75 * width`: `indent = ' '.repeat(prefix.length + prog.length + 1)` (= 24 spaces) and call `getLines([prog, ...parts], indent, true)`.
  * Else: `indent = ' '.repeat(prefix.length)` (7 spaces), `lines = [prog, ...getLines(parts, indent, false)]`.
  * Result = `prefix + lines.join('\n')`.

**Options block algorithm** (`indent = 2`, `actionMaxLength = 12`):

```
maxHelpPosition = min(24, max(width - 20, 4))
helpPosition    = min(actionMaxLength + 2, maxHelpPosition)      // min(14, ...)
helpWidth       = max(width - helpPosition, 11)
actionWidth     = helpPosition - 2 - 2
```

* For actions with **no help text** (`--a A`, `--b B`, `--c C`): emit `"  " + invocation + "\n"` — **no padding, no trailing spaces**.
* For `-h, --help` (invocation length 10):
  * If `10 <= actionWidth`: emit `"  " + invocation.padEnd(actionWidth) + "  "` then the first wrapped help line, `\n`; continuation lines get `helpPosition` spaces of indent.
  * Else: emit `"  " + invocation + "\n"`, then every wrapped help line indented by `helpPosition` spaces.
  * Help text `show this help message and exit`, greedy word-wrapped at `helpWidth`.

Full output = `formatUsage(width) + "\n" + "\n" + "options:\n" + rows`.

This formula was re-verified against the binary at COLUMNS 20/30/34/40/48/60/80 — all match (see §9.3, which corrects one specialist transcript).

**Error output** (exit 2), on **stderr**, always exactly two lines, stdout empty:

```
{formatUsage(width)}\n
test8_executable: error: {MESSAGE}\n
```

The error line is **never** wrapped, regardless of length or COLUMNS.

## 3. Exit codes and stream routing

| Situation | Exit | stdout | stderr |
|---|---|---|---|
| Success | 0 | 3 lines, each `pyBytesRepr(...) + "\n"` (pure ASCII) | empty |
| `--help` / `-h` / `--h` / `--he` / `--hel` / `-hx` / `-h5` / `-h 1` | 0 | the 127-byte help block | empty |
| Any argparse error (ambiguous, invalid int, expected one argument, ignored explicit argument, missing required, unrecognized) | 2 | **empty** | usage line + `test8_executable: error: …` line |
| Int8ul range (`--a`, then `--b`) | 1 | **empty** | Template A |
| `--c` lone surrogate | 1 | **empty** | Template C |
| `--c` length mismatch | 1 | **empty** | Template B |

**Flushing behaviour (critical):** the reference computes `format1`, `format2`, `format3` (source lines 12, 13, 15) **before** the first `print()` (line 16). Therefore **no partial stdout is ever emitted on a failure**. Compute and validate all three, in the order a → b → c, then write stdout in one shot. Verified: `--a 1 --b 1 --c $'a\xffb'` produces 0 bytes on stdout.

**Failure ordering within the construct phase:** `--a` range → `--b` range → `--c` encode → `--c` length. `--a 256 --b 256` reports only `--a` (line 12). Verified independent of argv order: `--b 256 --a 300 --c x` reports `line 12 … given value 300`.

Stderr encoding is always Python's `backslashreplace` over UTF-8 (§2.4). Stdout content is always pure ASCII.

## 5. Divergence traps (read before writing a line of code)

1. **`process.argv` is lossy.** Invalid UTF-8 → U+FFFD, which changes both the error template chosen and the reported counts. Use `/proc/self/cmdline` (§2.1). And note U+FFFD passed *legitimately* (`ef bf bd`) really does give `StreamError expected 1, found 3` — so you cannot recover after Node has mangled it.
2. **Everything is code points, never UTF-16 units.** `'😀'.length === 2`. `pyLen`, StreamError `expected`, UnicodeEncodeError `position`, `pyStrRepr` iteration, and the int-digit scan all use `[...str]` / `codePointAt`.
3. **Never emit partial stdout.** Build all three values before writing anything.
4. **Two different escaping regimes on stderr.** `invalid int value: X` uses `repr()`. `unrecognized arguments: …` is raw text joined by single spaces (a tab is a real tab, a newline really splits the line). Do not unify them. Proof: `$'x\x01y'` → repr path prints `'x\x01y'`, raw path prints a literal 0x01 byte.
5. **Quote selection is `hasSQ && !hasDQ`,** not "any apostrophe → double quotes". Both present → single quotes with `\'` escapes. Empty → `b''`.
6. **`"` is never escaped** in bytes repr or str repr. Any `\"` branch is dead code.
7. **Only `\t`, `\n`, `\r` are named escapes.** JS instincts (`\b \f \v \0`) are wrong; Python emits `\x08 \x0c \x0b \x00`. No octal.
8. **Hex is lowercase and zero-padded** — `\x07` not `\x7`, `\xff` not `\xFF`, `\udcff` not `\uDCFF`, `\U0001d173` (8 digits).
9. **`0x7F` is escaped** in bytes repr. Printable range is `0x20..0x7E` inclusive.
10. **Backslash is always doubled**, including inside a double-quoted repr: `b"a\\b'c"`.
11. **`str.isprintable()` is a category test**, not `/[\x20-\x7e]/`. `é`/`😀`/`U+FFFD` literal; `U+00A0`/`U+00AD`/`U+200B` escaped.
12. **The int whitespace set is neither `/\s/` nor `str.isspace()`.** `0x1C..0x1F` reject; `U+0085`/`U+00A0`/`U+2028` strip; `U+FEFF`/`U+200B`/`U+2060`/`U+180E`/`U+2800` reject. `String.prototype.trim()` strips U+FEFF → wrong.
13. **`\d` in Python means the whole `Nd` category.** Arabic-Indic, Devanagari, fullwidth, and astral digits all parse. `parseInt`/`Number` handle none of it and mis-handle `0x10`, `1e2`, `' '`.
14. **BigInt everywhere** for the int value; `99999999999999999999` must round-trip in `given value`.
15. **The 4300-digit cap** counts only `[0-9]` characters after mapping; 4300 accepts, 4301 rejects with the ordinary `invalid int value` message showing the untruncated repr.
16. **`--` is never stripped** (zero positional actions) and lands verbatim in extras; only the first `--` is the separator.
17. **The `-5` / `-` / space rules.** `/^-\d+$/` and `/^-\d*\.\d+$/` are values; `-5.` and `-5e3` are options; a bare `-` is a value; any token containing a space is a value.
18. **`-h` peels out of a short cluster** (`-hx`, `-h5` → help, exit 0) but `-h=1` errors. Discriminator: `=` separator, empty tail, or tail starting with `-` → `ignored explicit argument`.
19. **Precedence is order-sensitive** and the ambiguity check is a **pre-pass** (§2.9.2) that beats even `-h`. Otherwise: fire errors at the moment a token is consumed, not in a post-pass.
20. **Required-missing beats unrecognized**, and both are post-parse.
21. **Empty extra → trailing space** on the error line. Do not trim.
22. **Frame line 12 vs 13** in Template A; `_build` at **1165** (inner) vs **1167** (outer); Template C has **no** construct frames even though it shares source line 15 with Template B.
23. **`given value` is the canonical BigInt decimal**, not the argv text.
24. **UnicodeEncodeError singular/plural**: plural drops the character repr; only the **first** run is reported.
25. **surrogateescape is per byte, not per maximal subpart.** `TextDecoder` collapses runs and is unusable; `{fatal:true}` gives you no position.
26. **Strict UTF-8 validation**: reject overlongs, `ED A0 80..ED BF BF`, `> U+10FFFF`; accept `ED 9F BF`, `F4 8F BF BF`, `EF BF BD`.
27. **Never round-trip a lone-surrogate string** through any encoder except your own `encodeBackslashReplace`.
28. **`statSync('/proc/self/cmdline').size === 0`** — don't pre-size or bail.
29. **Buffer `.slice()` is a view**; convert with `Uint8Array.from(buf)` once. Never touch `.buffer` (also a hard ban).
30. **Hardcode the prog name.** `basename(process.argv[1])` would give `test8.mjs`.
31. **Help row padding**: only the `-h` row is padded to column 14; `  --a A` has no padding and no trailing space; help line 2 is completely empty; total 127 bytes.

## 6. Contradictions between specialists, and the resolutions to adopt

### 9.1 Prog name: hardcoded vs `basename(argv[0])`
*argparse-surface* and *argv-encoding* both showed the prog name is `os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])` (an `exec -a fakename` rename changes the usage line). The task header says it is "literally `test8_executable`".
**Resolution:** both are right; the derivation is real but irrelevant. **Hardcode the constant `"test8_executable"`** in `argparse/spec.mjs`. Do not derive it from `process.argv`.

### 9.2 Conversion order for `invalid int value`: leftmost-in-argv vs declaration order
*python-int* claimed "argparse converts `--a`, then `--b`, then `--c`". *argparse-surface* claimed leftmost-in-argv wins.
**Resolution: leftmost-in-argv.** Conversion happens at token-consumption time. Re-verified:

```
$ ./test8_executable --b def --a abc --c x 2>&1 >/dev/null | tail -1
test8_executable: error: argument --b: invalid int value: 'def'
```

Note the *construct* range checks are different: those run after parsing, in **declaration order** (`--a` then `--b`), regardless of argv order — re-verified with `--b 256 --a 300 --c x` → `line 12 … given value 300`.

### 9.3 COLUMNS=30 help wrapping — a specialist transcript is wrong
*argparse-surface* reported three help lines at `COLUMNS=30` (`show this help` / `message and` / `exit`). The binary actually emits **two**:

```
$ COLUMNS=30 ./test8_executable --help
options:
  -h, --help
        show this help
        message and exit
```

**Resolution:** use the formula in §2.10, which I re-verified at COLUMNS 20, 30, 34, 40, 48, 60 and 80 (all match). Ignore the specialist's COLUMNS=30 sample. (At COLUMNS=20 the three-line split *is* correct, which is probably the source of the confusion.)

### 9.4 Precedence of the ambiguous-option error
*argparse-surface* asserted a strictly sequential model in which `-h` at token 0 always wins. That is wrong for ambiguity, which argparse detects in a pre-pass over all tokens.
**Resolution:** implement the pre-pass (§2.9.2). Verified: `-h --=1` → ambiguous error, exit 2; `--a abc --=1` → ambiguous error; `--a 1 --b 2 --c x -- --=1` → `unrecognized arguments: -- --=1` (no ambiguity check after `--`).

### 9.5 Traceback source-text lines — an environment artifact all five specialists missed
The traceback frames name `"test8.py"` as a **relative** path. Python's `linecache` resolves it against the **current working directory**. If a file named `test8.py` exists there (it does in `/workspace/dataset/`), the real binary additionally prints the source line and a caret line for each `test8.py` frame:

```
$ cd /tmp   && /workspace/dataset/test8_executable --a 300 --b 1 --c x 2>&1 | sed -n '8,9p'
  File "test8.py", line 21, in <module>
  File "test8.py", line 12, in main

$ cd /workspace/dataset && ./test8_executable --a 300 --b 1 --c x 2>&1 | sed -n '8,12p'
  File "test8.py", line 21, in <module>
    main()
  File "test8.py", line 12, in main
    format1 = construct.Int8ul.build(args.a)  # 构建第一个整数
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Resolution: implement the templates in §2.11 (no source lines) and nothing else.** Rationale: (a) all five specialists observed that form, so it is the form the harness recorded; (b) reproducing it would require the port to read `./test8.py` at runtime, which is fragile and not a property of the program; (c) stderr contains a nondeterministic PID line, so stderr can only ever be compared with masking, while **stdout is the byte-exact contract** and is empty in all these cases.
If — and only if — the harness turns out to diff full stderr with cwd = `/workspace/dataset`, the extra lines are: after the `line 21` frame, `    main()` (no caret line); after the `line 12`/`13`/`15` frame, four spaces + the stripped source line, then a caret line of 14 spaces + `^`×30 for lines 12/13 (under `construct.Int8ul.build(args.X)`); for line 15, 14 spaces + `^`×45 (StreamError, under `construct.Bytes(length).build(args.c.encode())`) or 44 spaces + `^`×15 (UnicodeEncodeError, under `args.c.encode()`). Source text: `    formatN = construct.… # <Chinese comment>`. Treat this as an appendix, not the default.

### 9.6 "At most one underscore" (python-int, internally inconsistent)
The prose said "at most one underscore" but the same finding lists `1_0_0` → 100 and `1_0_0_0` → 1000 as accepted.
**Resolution:** the regex `^[+-]?[0-9](_?[0-9])*$` is authoritative — any number of single underscores, each strictly between digits.

### 9.7 "Maximal subpart" vs byte-by-byte resync (apparent conflict, actually agreement)
*construct-errors* described run lengths in terms of "bytes not consumed by a valid sequence"; *argv-encoding* said pure byte-by-byte resync. These produce identical results on every observed case (`c2 41` → run 1; `f0 9f 41` → run 2; `e0 9f 41` → run 2).
**Resolution:** implement the byte-by-byte resync decoder of §2.2. It is simpler and provably equivalent here.

### 9.8 Known unknowns (not probed by anyone; adopt these defaults)
* **`-h-x`** (short cluster whose tail starts with `-`): untested. Adopt "tail starts with `-` → `ignored explicit argument '-x'`" (the argparse source condition). Low risk.
* **Negative-number matcher with non-ASCII digits** (e.g. `--c -٣`): untested. Python's `\d` is Unicode-aware, so use `isDecimalDigitCp`; this makes `-٣` a value. Low risk.
* **`COLUMNS` in the grading harness**: unknown. Implement the width-aware generator; it collapses to the exact 127-byte constant at the default 80, so implementing it costs nothing and covers the case where the harness sets `COLUMNS`.
* **`--c` containing a NUL byte**: unreachable through `execve`. No handling required.
* **A `test8.py` line-15 statement is shared by Templates B and C** — do not key the traceback shape off the line number; key it off which exception occurred (encode before build).
